Executable: /workspace/dataset/test12_executable
Source (Python, for reference):
    import argparse
    from furl import furl
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--b', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--c', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--d', type=str, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    f = furl(args.a)
    print(f.fragment.__setattr__('str', args.b) or f.fragment)   # LINE1
    print(f.fragment.add(args.c))                                # LINE2
    print(f.fragment.set(args.d, 'value'))                       # LINE3
    print(f.url)                                                 # LINE4

RUN IT LIKE: /workspace/dataset/test12_executable --a "<A>" --b "<B>" --c "<C>" --d "<D>"
Never use the 'python' command. Do not read furl source; it is not available. Probe empirically.

ALREADY-ESTABLISHED FACTS (do not re-derive, but DO stress-test if in your area):
- --b is completely ignored: __setattr__('str', b) sets a dead instance attribute, no effect, returns None.
- LINE1 prints str(fragment) as parsed from A.
- LINE2 = fragment.path.add(C) then print str(fragment).
- LINE3 = fragment.path.load(D); fragment.query.load('value'); print str(fragment)  -> query is always literally 'value'.
- LINE4 prints the whole URL with the mutated fragment.
- Fragment str = path + '?' + query when both non-empty, else path+query. When query non-empty, literal '?' chars inside the fragment PATH are escaped to %3F; when query is empty they stay raw.
- furl DECODES percent-escapes on parse and RE-ENCODES on output: '%41%42' -> 'AB'; '%2F' inside a path segment -> stays '%2F'; lone '%' -> '%25'; 'a%zz' -> 'a%25zz'.
- Scheme and host are lowercased. Default ports dropped (http:80, https:443) but non-default kept (http:443 kept).
- URL query: '+' decodes to space, space encodes to '+'. 'a=b&c&d=' round-trips exactly (key-only 'c' vs empty-value 'd=' are distinct).

METHOD: run MANY probes (60+), vary one thing at a time, use printf %q or cat -A style to make whitespace visible, and note exit codes and stderr separately. Prefer a bash loop over a case list.

DELIVERABLE: a precise, implementable specification of YOUR assigned area: exact algorithm/rules, character sets (list the literal safe characters), ordering of operations, and a table of at least 25 concrete input->output examples you actually observed (verbatim). Call out anything surprising or that you could not determine. Be rigorous: an implementer will code directly from your spec with no access to the executable.


AREA: the FRAGMENT path: how fragment.path is parsed from A's '#...' portion, how .add(C) appends, how .load(D) replaces, and how segments are encoded in LINE1/LINE2/LINE3/LINE4.
Determine the SAFE character set for FRAGMENT path segments and how it differs from the main URL path (test every ASCII punctuation char inside C and inside D and inside A's fragment).
Nail down .add() semantics precisely:
- add to empty path, add to path with trailing slash, add absolute-looking '/x', add '', add '/', add 'a/b/c', add 'a//b', add '.' and '..'.
- Does add join with '/' always? What happens with trailing-slash bookkeeping (e.g. fragment 'a/' + add 'b' -> 'a/b', fragment 'a' + add 'b' -> 'a/b', fragment 'a' + add '/b' -> ?).
- Is the result of add() the same object printed later (mutation) — confirm LINE3 fully replaces the path from LINE2.
Also characterize .load(D): does it reset absolute/trailing-slash state? Is the leading '/' preserved ('/x' -> '/x?value')?
And confirm the '?'-escaping rule: '?' raw when fragment query empty, '%3F' when query non-empty — test in LINE2 with an A whose fragment already has a query, and in LINE3 (query always 'value'). Does the same conditional escaping apply to any OTHER character (e.g. '#')?

input.area: FRAGMENT path: parsing of A's "#..." into fragment.path, .add(C) append semantics, .load(D) replacement, and per-segment percent-encoding in LINE1/LINE2/LINE3/LINE4
rules: PRE-PASS ON A (whole URL): before any parsing, every TAB (0x09), LF (0x0A) and CR (0x0D) byte is deleted from A (Python urlsplit behaviour). Verified: A='http://x.com/p#a<TAB>b' -> LINE1 'ab'. This stripping does NOT happen for C or D (C=D='a<TAB>b' -> 'a%09b').
FRAGMENT EXTRACTION: frag_raw = everything in (stripped) A after the FIRST '#'. If A has no '#', frag_raw = '' . '#' characters after the first one stay inside frag_raw (they later encode to %23).

FRAGMENT SPLIT HEURISTIC (operates on the RAW, still-percent-encoded frag_raw; this decides path vs query and is the only place '?' and '=' are looked at literally): let i = index of first literal '?' in frag_raw. (a) if i exists AND frag_raw[i+1:] contains a literal '=' -> path_raw = frag_raw[:i], query_raw = frag_raw[i+1:]. (b) else if i exists (no '=' after the '?') -> path_raw = frag_raw (the WHOLE fragment, '?' included), query_raw = ''. (c) else (no '?') if frag_raw contains '=' -> path_raw = '', query_raw = frag_raw. (d) else -> path_raw = frag_raw, query_raw = ''. Examples: 'a?b'->path 'a?b'; 'a?b=c'->path 'a', query 'b=c'; 'a=b'->path '', query 'a=b'; 'a=b?c'->path 'a=b?c'; 'a=b?c=d'->path 'a=b', query 'c=d'; '?'->path '?'; '?='->path '', query '='. Because the test is on the raw text, '%3D' does NOT count as '=' ('a%3Db' -> path) and '%3F' does not count as '?' ('%3F' -> path '%3F' which then decodes to '?').

QUERY-NON-EMPTY FLAG (qne): qne = (query_raw != '') for LINE1/LINE2; for LINE3/LINE4 the query is always the literal string 'value', so qne = true. qne only affects whether '?' is emitted raw or as %3F inside path segments (see rule 8).

PATH REPRESENTATION: a path string is split on literal '/' into segments (Python str.split('/'), so 'a/b'->['a','b'], ''->[''], '/'->['',''], 'a/'->['a','']). Each segment is independently normalised: DECODE-OR-LITERAL then ENCODE (rules 6-8). Segments are re-joined with '/'. No '.'/'..' normalisation and no collapsing of empty segments ever happens ('a/../b' and 'a//b' and 'a/.' survive verbatim).

PER-SEGMENT DECODE-OR-LITERAL: a segment is 'already-valid-encoded' iff it fully matches ^(?:[A-Za-z0-9!$&'()*+,\-.:;=@_~]|[^\x00-\x7F]|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})*$ (i.e. only path-safe ASCII chars, bytes >= 0x80, and complete %HH escapes). If VALID: percent-unescape it (%HH -> that byte; other chars keep their UTF-8 bytes) to get the stored byte string. If INVALID: the segment's raw UTF-8 bytes are stored verbatim (its '%' will later be re-encoded to %25). Note '?' is NOT in the valid set even though '?' may be emitted raw: segment '%3F' is VALID -> stores '?' ; segment '%3F?k' is INVALID -> stores the literal 8 chars '%3F?k' -> prints '%253F?k'. Other examples: '%2f'->VALID->stores '/'; 'a%b'->INVALID; '%4'->INVALID; '%2G'->INVALID; '%41é'->VALID->stores 'Aé'.

ENCODING OUTPUT (per stored segment, byte by byte): a byte is emitted literally iff it is one of A-Z a-z 0-9 ! $ & ' ( ) * + , - . : ; = @ _ ~ , OR it is 0x3F ('?') and qne is false. Every other byte (space, ", #, %, <, >, [, \, ], ^, `, {, |, }, all C0 controls, 0x7F, all bytes >= 0x80, and '/' which can only appear inside a stored segment via %2F) becomes '%' + 2 UPPERCASE hex digits. So: ' '->%20, '"'->%22, '#'->%23, '%'->%25, '/'->%2F, '<'->%3C, '>'->%3E, '?'->%3F (only when qne), '['->%5B, '\\'->%5C, ']'->%5D, '^'->%5E, '`'->%60, '{'->%7B, '|'->%7C, '}'->%7D, 'é'->%C3%A9. Hex is always normalised to uppercase ('%2f'->'%2F', '%c3%a9'->'%C3%A9').

CONDITIONAL '?' ESCAPING is the ONLY conditional character: with an empty fragment query a '?' in the fragment path prints raw; with a non-empty fragment query it prints %3F. Verified in LINE2 (A='#p?q=1', C='a?b' -> 'p/a%3Fb?q=1' vs A='#p?q', C='a?b' -> 'p?q/a?b') and in LINE3 (query always 'value' -> D='a?b' -> 'a%3Fb?value'). '#' is ALWAYS %23; '=', '&', ';', '+', ':' etc. are always raw; nothing else changes with qne.

LINE1 = str(fragment) where path = normalise(path_raw) (rules 5-8, qne from rule 4) and query = normalised query_raw. str(fragment) = path if query=='' ; = query if path=='' ; = path + '?' + query if both non-empty.

LINE2 = fragment.path.add(C) then str(fragment). ADD ALGORITHM (all on the already-encoded string forms; equivalently on segment lists). Let cur = the current ENCODED path string (LINE1's path part) and cnew = normalise(C) (C is split on its own literal '/' characters and each segment encoded as in rules 5-8; a '/' produced by decoding %2F is NOT a separator). Then: abs = cur.startswith('/'); cur1 = cur[1:] if abs else cur; r = relJoin(cur1, cnew); if abs and r != '' and not r.startswith('/'): r = '/' + r; new path = r. Where relJoin(x,y): if x=='' return y; if y=='' return x; if x.endswith('/') or y.startswith('/') return x+y; return x+'/'+y.

CONSEQUENCES OF RULE 10 (all verified over the full 12x8 cur/C matrix): join is with exactly one '/' only when neither side already supplies one — 'a'+'b'->'a/b', 'a/'+'b'->'a/b', 'a'+'/b'->'a/b', 'a/'+'/b'->'a//b'. add('') is a no-op ('a'+''->'a'), add('/') appends a trailing slash ('a'+'/'->'a/'), add on an empty path yields C verbatim (''+'/b'->'/b', ''+'b'->'b'). SURPRISING: for an ABSOLUTE current path one leading '/' is consumed by cur1=cur[1:] and only re-added if the join result is not already absolute, so leading-slash runs shrink: '//'+'x'->'/x', '///'+'x'->'//x', '////'+'x'->'///x', '//a'+'b'->'/a/b', '///a'+'b'->'//a/b', '//a//'+'b'->'/a//b', and '/'+''->'' (an absolute path can lose its leading slash entirely), while '/a'+'b'->'/a/b' and '/a//'+'b'->'/a//b' are unchanged.
MUTATION: add() mutates the same fragment/path object that LINE1 printed, so LINE2 shows A's fragment path with C appended and A's fragment query unchanged.

LINE3 = fragment.path.load(D); fragment.query.load('value'); str(fragment). load() DISCARDS the LINE2 path completely (nothing from A or C survives) and stores normalise(D) with qne=true. load() fully resets absolute/trailing-slash state from D alone: D='/x' -> '/x?value', D='//x' -> '//x?value', D='x/' -> 'x/?value', D='/' -> '/?value', D='/e/f/' -> '/e/f/?value', D='' -> path empty so LINE3 is just 'value'. D is never split on '?' (D='d?e' -> path 'd?e' -> printed 'd%3Fe?value').

LINE4 = the whole URL with this final fragment: it is exactly (everything of A before the '#', re-canonicalised by the non-fragment rules) + '#' + LINE3. The '#' is present whenever LINE3 is non-empty (it always is, since the query is 'value').

DIFFERENCE FROM THE MAIN URL PATH: the literal-safe byte set is IDENTICAL (A-Za-z0-9 ! $ & ' ( ) * + , - . : ; = @ _ ~ plus '/' as separator; same 12 punctuation chars encoded). The only difference is the conditional raw '?': the fragment path prints '?' unescaped when the fragment query is empty, whereas in the main URL path a '?' can only ever appear as %3F (A='http://x.com/a%3Fb' -> LINE4 'http://x.com/a%3Fb#value'). The valid-encoded-segment predicate and the decode-then-re-encode behaviour appear to be the same code path (furl.py _segments_from_path) for both.

ERROR CASE: bytes in A, C or D that are not valid UTF-8 (e.g. a lone 0xFF) cause an uncaught UnicodeEncodeError traceback from furl.py:_segments_from_path / urllib.parse.quote and exit code 1, with no stdout.
